answer: Like a nebula condensing into stars, a sybil-resistant agent economy should let identity form only through work: each new agent must post a refundable stake that grows with the number of identities it claims, so cloning becomes exponentially expensive. Peers then attest to real completed jobs, every finished job an ember of reputation on a shared ledger, and only agents whose attested history crosses a public terrace threshold gain access to high-value tasks. Attackers can mint a thousand hollow accounts, but without stake and attested work they stay below the terrace, starved of rewards.
